about.name: Md Shariful Islam Rayhan
about.title: Computer Science & Engineering Student
about.tagline: Building systems, leading communities, and turning ideas into software.
about.summary: Final-year CSE student at University of Dhaka with hands-on experience in backend development, system programming, and building scalable applications. President of CSEDU Students' Club, leading 200+ members and organizing hackathons and AI competitions.

education.degree: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Engineering

projects.title: Physics Mechanical Calculator
projects.description: Interactive calculator using SDL framework for physics and mechanical engineering problems. Implements animations to visualize engineering concepts alongside computational logic.

projects.title: Bookly – Android App
projects.description: Android application for buying books with user rating system, search functionality, and contact modules.

projects.title: Marketplace Web Application
projects.description: Flask-based backend handling business logic and REST APIs. Applied modular architecture for maintainability and scalability.

projects.title: Hospital Management System
projects.description: Terminal-based database system using MySQL. Uses indexing, triggers, stored procedures, and views for optimized performance. Implements patient records, appointments, and administrative modules.

projects.title: NetConnect – Terminal Group Chat
projects.description: Terminal-based group chat for multiple concurrent users. Implements group creation, member management, approval-based joining, and efficient networking protocols for real-time communication.

highlights: Led a 200+ member organization; coordinated seminars, workshops, and cultural activities.
Organized and led Code Samurai Hackathon with nearly 50 teams, in collaboration with CSEDU and leading Japanese software companies.
Led VisionX-2025, an AI-based competition hosted by CSEDU.
Facilitated technical workshops, seminars, and cultural events to enhance student engagement and learning.
